title: Agent Orchestration Schema
description: As-is schema of the 3-gate propose/apply pipeline plus a bounded re-plan loop (adopted 2026-07-24, same-day FOURTH revision): Opus-high plan/spec v1 -> orchestrator implements inline -> Gate 1 (Sonnet-medium critic, propose-if-confident) -> Gate 2 (Opus-low, propose) -> Gate 3 (Opus-medium, direct write) -> ladder exhausted -> Opus-high ALWAYS re-plans (v2, NEVER fixes code) -> orchestrator implements v2 -> Opus-medium direct fix if needed (no critic, no Gate 2) -> Opus-high re-plans once more (v3, TERMINAL) -> orchestrator implements v3 -> Opus-medium direct fix if needed -> STOP. Gates 1-2 never apply their own fixes; the orchestrator (already Sonnet-low) applies verbatim and reruns the exact check, avoiding an extra subagent spawn. Corrected same day (revision 4): an earlier draft let opus_planner 'repair OR re-scope' at the terminal step, which the user explicitly rejected — opus_planner must NEVER write or apply code, in any mode, at any round; its only output is a plan/spec, and the re-plan loop is bounded to 2 rounds with a lighter orchestrator+opus_fixer_med retry each round (no Gate 1/2, since the original plan is the more likely defect once the full ladder failed). Sources: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules/orchestration.md, agents/*.md, plus live Anthropic pricing (2026-07-24 web search) and the observed runtime environment. Fields are provenance-tagged: [docs] = documented policy, [observed] = runtime state, [priced] = confirmed against live rate card. Doc/runtime disagreements live in 'discrepancies', not silently resolved.

orchestrator.description: The session model itself — not a spawnable subagent, but the universal fix-executor for Gates 1-2. Source: CLAUDE.md 'Model Hierarchy'.

model.description: [docs] pin the role to claude-sonnet-5 at low effort; [observed] set via /model on 2026-07-24 (resolves prior discrepancy D1).

agents.description: Spawnable subagents registered in agents/*.md. Exactly these four. Per-agent 'effort' is set via the supported frontmatter key (verified: low|medium|high|xhigh|max, overrides session effort). Opus backs three distinct effort tiers. opus_fixer_med has two invocation contexts (see its invoke_for) but is still one agent definition, not two.

role.const: direct-write fixer, TWO contexts: Gate 3 (original plan) and post-replan retry

const: Read

Context A (Gate 3, original plan): escalation only, after Gate 2's proposed fix (applied by the orchestrator) also failed — two propose/apply cycles already failed, indirection stops earning its cost. Writes AND applies the fix directly, reruns the check itself, ONE shot. On failure, escalates to opus_planner (which re-plans).

Context B (post-replan retry): invoked directly after the orchestrator implements a re-planned spec (v2 or v3) — NO critic, NO Gate 2 this round, since the original plan (not a fresh implementation bug) was the more likely defect. Writes and applies directly, ONE shot. On failure in round 1 (v2), escalates back to opus_planner for a second re-plan (v3, terminal); on failure in round 2 (v3), escalates to STOP.

routing.description: Ordered decision tree — first matching rule wins. Source: rules/orchestration.md 'Decision Tree'.

const.condition: fully enumerable edits, no design judgment

const.route: opus_planner [high] -> orchestrator implement (inline, or opus_fixer_med at orchestrator's discretion) -> sonnet_critic [medium] Gate 1

escalation.description: Three quality gates on the original plan, then a bounded re-plan loop (max 2 rounds) with a lighter retry each round. Gates 1-2 are propose/orchestrator-applies; opus_fixer_med is the sole direct-write agent (both contexts). opus_planner NEVER fixes code in any mode — its only terminal action is producing a new plan. Never skip a gate or round in either direction; the pipeline never loops beyond the 2-round bound.

const.action: sonnet_critic [medium] proposes IF confident; orchestrator [low, inline] applies verbatim + reruns the exact check (or skips straight to rung 2 if no confident proposal)
opus_fixer_low [low] proposes (cross-model); orchestrator [low, inline] applies verbatim + reruns
opus_fixer_med [medium], Context A: writes AND applies directly, ONE shot, no intermediary — reruns itself
opus_planner [high] ALWAYS re-plans (v2) — NEVER attempts a fix. This is re-plan round 1 of a max-2-round bound.
orchestrator [low, inline] implements v2 from the new spec
opus_fixer_med [medium], Context B: writes AND applies directly, ONE shot — NO critic, NO Gate 2 this round (lighter retry; the original plan was the more likely defect)
opus_planner [high] re-plans AGAIN (v3) — this is re-plan round 2, EXPLICITLY TERMINAL, must state so
orchestrator [low, inline] implements v3 from the new spec
opus_fixer_med [medium], Context B: writes AND applies directly, ONE shot — NO critic, NO Gate 2
STOP — report to user with full evidence trail. NO third re-plan; the bound is hard.

correction.const: 2026-07-24, same-day fourth revision: an earlier draft had opus_planner 'repair OR re-scope' as its terminal action (rungs 4/7 above). The user explicitly rejected this — opus_planner must ALWAYS re-plan, NEVER fix code, in any mode, at any round. The re-plan loop's bound (max 2 rounds) and its lighter retry shape (orchestrator + opus_fixer_med Context B only, no critic, no Gate 2) were specified by the user in the same correction.

pricing.description: [priced, 2026-07-24 web search] Live Anthropic API rates per million tokens, grounding the gate-order rationale. Effort tiers (low/medium/high) do NOT change the per-token rate — only how many reasoning tokens get generated at that rate.

opus_vs_sonnet_ratio.const: ~2.5x during Sonnet intro pricing, ~1.67x after — not the 5-10x gap of older Claude generations

design_implication.const: the 3-gate order optimizes for 'does this tier meaningfully raise the odds of a fix,' not dollar-avoidance — a same-family critique (Gate 1) is a genuinely different, often-sufficient check before paying for a cross-model read (Gate 2), and collapsing the apply step into the orchestrator (no extra spawn) is free regardless of per-token cost

discrepancies.description: Doc-vs-runtime mismatches, surfaced not resolved — a spec/reality disagreement is a defect to resolve explicitly, and resolving these is the user's call.
